newsitem.title: USA: Wheat prices rise ahead of sales to India, Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Wheat prices rise ahead of sales to India, Egypt.

text.p: Wheat prices rose Tuesday ahead of expected sales to Egypt and India, while orange juice rose again on worries of freeze damage in Florida.
Gold and silver prices tumbled because higher stock prices may siphon investor support away from the metals.

U.S. grain exporters said India was immediately seeking 50,000 to 750,000 metric tons of wheat, and Egypt wanted 50,000 tons or more. U.S. exporters said some of the demand may be filled by U.S. wheat.
"India will be in tonight for wheat. They're saying 50,000 but it could be up to 750,000 tons, it's an open-ended tender," a trader said.

Also talk in U.S. wheat markets Tuesday claimed India found problems with the quality of some Canadian wheat. Indian and Canandian grain officials denied this, but the denials failed to discourage bullish U.S. wheat traders who said the alleged problems could boost sales of U.S. wheat.

At the Chicago Board of Trade, soft red winter wheat for March delivery closed up 1-1/2 cents at $3.73 per bushel, and the July contract, which reflects the price at harvest, rose 3 cents to $3.47-1/4.
At the Kansas City Board of Trade, hard red winter wheat closed up 2-1/4 cents for March delivery at $4.18-1/2.

Frozen concentrated orange juice prices closed higher in nearby months at New York's Cotton Exchange but sharply higher in later months for the second consecutive day as fears persisted that a recent cold spell damaged Florida oranges.
The Florida Department of Agriculture put losses to the state's citrus crop at $60 million, but there was no official damage estimate, a spokesman for the department said.
Concerns that cold weather forecast to hit Florida this weekend could increase prior freeze damage may have contributed to the higher prices.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said temperatures should remain in the mid 30s (F), well above the level that would damage the fruit.
The March contract closed up 0.25 cent to 93.75 cents a pound, but was sharply higher during the session, peaking at 99.00, the highest level since Dec. 5.

A sharp rebound in U.S. stock and bond markets and a higher dollar sent gold and silver prices tumbling at New York's Commodity Exchange, as traders believed the stocks will pull investors away from precious metals.
"Prospects that a low inflation environment will support higher equity values suggest that disinvestment of gold will remain in vogue in 1997," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
The dollar hit a 31-month high against the Gemran mark and a 47-month high against the Japanese yen Tuesday.
February gold at the New York Mercantile Exchange's Comex divsion ended down $3.30 an ounce at $354.00, and March silver ended down 8.4 cents an ounce Tuesday at $4.963.

Oil prices slipped in lackluster trading at the New York Mercantile Exchange as traders doubted there would be surprises in oil inventory data released after the close Tuesday from the American Petroleum Institute.
February heating oil and gasoline both finished lower as dealers rolled positions into the March contract ahead of the February contract expiry for refined products on Friday.
March crude oil closed down 4 cents at $23.90 per barrel, February heating oil was off 0.46 cent at 66.83 cents per gallon, and February gasoline was off 0.58 cent at 67.04 cents per gallon.
